spec_points.description: Convert between denary, binary, and hexadecimal number representations
Perform binary addition and subtraction; use two's complement for negative numbers
Understand overflow and its detection
Represent and manipulate binary fractions; understand fixed-point and floating-point formats
Understand normalisation of floating-point numbers; explain rounding errors and underflow/overflow
Know ASCII and Unicode character encoding; understand the need for Unicode
Describe how images are represented using pixels, bit depth, resolution, and colour depth
Describe how sound is represented using sampling rate, sample resolution, and the ADC process
Describe lossless and lossy compression; explain run-length encoding (RLE)
Describe LAN, WAN, and the Internet; distinguish between bus, star, and mesh topologies
Understand client-server and peer-to-peer models
Explain the purpose of protocols: TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP, SMTP, POP3
Describe the TCP/IP four-layer model; explain the role of each layer
Explain symmetric and asymmetric encryption; describe public and private key use
Describe digital certificates and digital signatures
Identify common security threats: malware, phishing, man-in-the-middle, SQL injection
Describe firewall types, intrusion detection, and other security measures
Describe the von Neumann architecture: ALU, CU, registers, buses
Explain the fetch-decode-execute cycle in detail
Understand factors affecting processor performance: clock speed, cores, cache, pipelining
Describe RISC vs CISC architectures; understand Harvard architecture
Distinguish between RAM and ROM; describe the memory hierarchy
Explain the purpose of cache memory (L1, L2, L3) and virtual memory
Compare primary, secondary, and tertiary storage; compare storage media (HDD, SSD, optical)
Describe the functions of an operating system: process management, memory management, file management
Explain process scheduling algorithms: round robin, shortest job first, priority scheduling
Understand interrupts and their role in processor management
Distinguish between assemblers, compilers, and interpreters
Describe the stages of compilation: lexical analysis, syntax analysis, semantic analysis, code generation, optimisation
Understand the role of a linker and a loader
Decompose a problem into smaller sub-problems
Apply abstraction to identify relevant features and ignore irrelevant detail
Construct structure diagrams, flowcharts, and pseudocode to represent algorithms
Implement and analyse linear search and binary search
Implement and analyse bubble sort and merge sort
Trace recursive algorithms; write recursive solutions for standard problems
Express time complexity using Big-O notation: O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²)
Use 1D and 2D arrays; traverse, search, and update elements
Describe and implement singly-linked and doubly-linked lists: insertion, deletion, traversal
Compare arrays and linked lists for different use cases
Describe and implement a stack using an array; implement push, pop, peek, isEmpty
Describe and implement a queue (linear and circular) using an array
Apply stacks to: function call management, expression evaluation (postfix), undo operations
Apply queues to: scheduling, I/O buffering, breadth-first search
Describe the structure of binary trees; implement insertion and search
Perform and implement pre-order, in-order, and post-order tree traversal
Describe hash tables: hash functions, collision resolution (chaining, open addressing)
Analyse worst-case and average-case performance of hash table operations
Use variables, constants, data types, assignment, arithmetic and Boolean expressions
Use sequence, selection (IF, CASE/SWITCH), and iteration (FOR, WHILE, REPEAT-UNTIL)
Define and call procedures and functions; understand parameter passing (by value and reference)
Understand scope: local vs global variables
Open, read, write, and close text files in programs
Handle runtime errors using exception handling constructs (try/except)
Construct and simplify truth tables for logic circuits
Apply Boolean algebra laws (De Morgan's theorems, absorption, etc.) to simplify expressions
Use Karnaugh maps to simplify Boolean expressions
Describe flip-flops (SR, D, JK) and their use in registers
Describe imperative, object-oriented, declarative, and functional programming paradigms
Understand OOP concepts: classes, objects, encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism
Describe declarative programming and logical deduction (Prolog-style)
Understand functional programming: higher-order functions, map, filter, reduce, immutability
Understand the relational data model: tables, primary keys, foreign keys
Normalise tables to 1NF, 2NF, and 3NF
Write SQL queries: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, JOIN, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
Understand the role of a DBMS; describe ACID properties of transactions
Describe AI problem-solving approaches: graph traversal (BFS, DFS), A* algorithm
Understand machine learning: training data, supervised vs unsupervised learning
Describe neural networks at a high level: neurons, layers, weights, activation functions
Discuss ethical and social implications of AI
Represent graphs using adjacency matrices and adjacency lists
Implement depth-first search (DFS) and breadth-first search (BFS)
Apply Dijkstra's algorithm to find shortest paths
Describe minimum spanning trees; apply Prim's and Kruskal's algorithms
Define and implement abstract data types: list, stack, queue, dictionary, graph
Choose appropriate data structures for specific problems with justification
Design class hierarchies using inheritance; implement abstract classes and interfaces
Apply polymorphism through method overriding
Use UML class diagrams to model object-oriented systems
Design and implement OOP solutions to substantial problems
